items.heading: Do You Want a Government
items.text: Do You Want a Government Do you want a government-gated door or a private-sector door. Archives, ASI, civil services, and NET-based teaching all run through structured government exams and fixed vacancy cycles. Journalism, publishing, corporate roles, and heritage tourism run through private hiring, portfolios, and certifications instead.

items.heading: Do You Want Fieldwork Do
items.text: Do You Want Fieldwork Do Do You Want Fieldwork Do you want fieldwork or desk work. Archaeology and heritage tourism are physically active and site-based. Archives, research, and content roles are largely desk-bound. Most people already know which one drains them and which one energises them.

CLAT has no age limit and unlimited attempts. Top NLU graduates can start above Rs 15-18 LPA; tier-2 and tier-3 law college outcomes are far more modest. Independent practice later on is a genuine ownership path with no fixed pay ceiling.
Corporate and generalist roles (content, HR, business analysis)
Graduates who want faster, non-exam entry into stable private-sector income.

History alone rarely opens these doors. A multiplier skill (writing systems, data basics, communication training) has to sit on top of the degree, but the pay ceiling here is often the highest of all nine paths once you specialise.
Graduates who write well and want their history knowledge to show up as public work, not a filing cabinet of facts.

Entry-level reporter, editorial, and documentary-research roles typically start around Rs 2.5-5 LPA. A visible portfolio matters more than a mass-communication credential, and freelance or own-byline work can scale well beyond a single employer's pay band.
Graduates who like direct public interaction and storytelling more than desk-bound research.
The Ministry of Tourism runs a formal 330-hour Heritage Tour Guide certification and a 420-hour Regional Level Guide course, open to candidates 18-28 with at least Class 10.

items.heading: Can You Commit to Another
items.text: Can you commit to another degree, or do you need to start earning sooner. Archives, museums, archaeology, and academia effectively require an MA and often a diploma on top of it. Heritage tourism guiding and entry-level content or journalism roles are the two paths on this list that do not strictly require another postgraduate degree first.

items.heading: Do You Want to Stay
items.text: Do you want to stay inside history itself, or use it as a base for something adjacent. Archives, museums, archaeology, teaching, and research keep you working directly with historical material. Law, journalism, corporate communications, and civil services use the reading, writing, and reasoning skill a history degree builds, but apply it to a different subject entirely.
